headline: PSEi Closes at 5,916.94, Falling Below 6,000
seoTitle: PSEi Closes Below 6,000 at 5,916.94 | FMB News
seoDescription: The Philippine Stock Exchange index closed at 5,916.94 on September 16, down 90.84 points or 1.51%, according to official PSE market data.
deck: Official Philippine Stock Exchange data show the benchmark index ended Wednesday at 5,916.94, down 90.84 points or 1.51%. The close confirms the index moved below the 6,000 level after finishing the previous session just above it.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Philippine Stock Exchange index closed Wednesday at 5,916.94, down 90.84 points or 1.51%, according to the Philippine Stock Exchange's official index summary.
The broader All Shares index fell 42.26 points or 1.26% to 3,300.26. The PSE recorded 139 declining issues, 54 advances and 58 unchanged issues, with total value turnover of about P5.89 billion.

sections.heading: What is confirmed
paragraphs: The PSE's official market summary marked the market closed as of 4:26 p.m. on September 16 and reported the PSEi at 5,916.94. This is the authoritative closing level used by FMB News.

Independent reporting from the Philippine Daily Inquirer and The Philippine Star also reported the index's move below 6,000 and cited concerns including the domestic growth outlook, currency and inflation risks, elevated oil prices and uncertainty ahead of U.S. monetary-policy decisions.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The PSEi had closed the previous trading day at 6,007.78, leaving the benchmark close to the 6,000 threshold before Wednesday's decline. The latest close therefore represents a confirmed break below that level rather than an intraday move alone.
Market commentary about why investors bought or sold shares represents analysis by market participants and news organizations, not a single officially established cause of the decline.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The PSEi tracks a basket of major listed Philippine companies and is widely used as a benchmark for the domestic equity market. A sharp move can affect portfolio values and provide a snapshot of investor risk appetite, although one trading session does not by itself establish a longer-term economic trend.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch the next trading session for whether the index remains below 6,000, foreign-fund flows, movements in the peso and oil prices, and any change in global interest-rate expectations. FMB News will treat subsequent market moves as new developments only when they are independently consequential.
